{{Short description|American chemist (1928–2021)}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=July 2025}}
'''Daryle Hadley Busch''' (March 30, 1928  –  May 19, 2021) was an American inorganic chemist.<ref>{{cite web |title=Daryle H. Busch |url=https://obituaries.ljworld.com/obituaries/ljworld/obituary.aspx?n=daryle-h-busch&pid=198725469&fhid=24990 |publisher=Lawrence Journal-World |access-date=3 June 2021}}</ref>

A native of [[Carterville, Illinois]], born in 1928, Busch attended [[Southern Illinois University]] and earned a master's, and doctorate in chemistry from the [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign|University of Illinois]].<ref name="tribute">{{cite journal|authorlink1=John C. Bailar Jr. |last1=Bailar Jr. |first1=John C. |last2=Busch |first2=Daryle H. |title=Tribute to Professor Daryle Busch |journal=Journal of Coordination Chemistry |date=1988 |volume=19 |issue=1–3 |pages=iv |doi=10.1080/00958972.1988.9728138}}</ref><ref name="siu">{{cite news |title=Daryle H. Busch |url=https://chem.siu.edu/alumni/hall-of-fame/busch.php |access-date=16 December 2018 |publisher=Southern Illinois University}}</ref> Upon graduation, he began teaching at the [[Ohio State University]]. Busch was awarded a Guggenheim fellowship in 1981.<ref>{{cite news |title=Daryle H. Busch |url=https://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/daryle-h-busch/ |access-date=16 December 2018 |publisher=John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation}}</ref> He retired from OSU in 1988, a year after he had been appointed to a presidential professorship.<ref name="siu"/> Busch then joined the [[University of Kansas]] faculty as Roy A. Roberts Distinguished Professor of Chemistry.<ref name="siu"/><ref>{{cite news |title=Daryle H. Busch |url=https://chem.ku.edu/people/faculty/dbusch |access-date=16 December 2018 |publisher=University of Kansas |archive-date=December 16, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181216163422/https://chem.ku.edu/people/faculty/dbusch |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was president of the [[American Chemical Society]] in 2000.
